gaps.gap: Thin, low-schema content on high-impression review pages (/review/gesture/ at 2,672 impressions, /review/leap-plus/ at 1,046, /review/aeron-size-c/ at 723) is suppressing CTR and blocking top-5 rankings. ChairsFX ranks with a ~14,684-word Aeron review using Article + Product + Person schema; our reviews are almost certainly far shorter with no structured data.
gaps.recommendation: This week: expand /review/gesture/ to 3,000–5,000 words with tall-person-specific sections (seat height range, seat depth for long legs, back height for 6'+ torsos, weight capacity), add a spec comparison table, and implement Article + Product + Review + BreadcrumbList schema. Mirror this treatment for /review/leap-plus/ and /review/aeron-size-c/. Even a 2-position SERP jump on /review/gesture/ alone could 3-4x clicks from that impression pool.

gaps.gap: /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ sits at position 22.3 with 687 impressions — our flagship money page is buried on page 2–3. Tall.Life ranks for this exact query with only ~3,795 words and no Product schema, meaning the barrier to overtake them is low. BTOD dominates with a broad 'big and tall' page at ~7,603 words. We have no page competing at their content depth, and we have the niche authority advantage they don't.
gaps.recommendation: Prioritize a full rewrite/expansion of /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ to 4,000–6,000 words this week. Structure it around: (1) why standard chairs fail at 6'+ with biomechanical reasoning, (2) a filterable comparison table of chairs by max seat height, seat depth, and weight capacity, (3) H2s targeting tall-specific sub-queries ('office chairs for 6'4', 'chairs with high seat height adjustment', 'deep seat office chair for long legs'), and (4) ItemList + Product + FAQPage schema. This directly attacks the gap Tall.Life owns weakly and BTOD owns without tall-specific authority.

gaps.gap: /correct-chair-dimensions/ and /knee-pain-seat-depth/ together generate 3,793 impressions at positions 15.8 and 8.6 respectively but convert almost nothing (0.17% and 0.15% CTR). These are informational queries where Wirecutter (~24,571 words, full schema suite) and ChairsFX dominate. Our pages likely lack the depth, internal linking to money pages, and schema to earn featured snippets or rich results that would lift CTR at these positions.
gaps.recommendation: Merge or cross-link /correct-chair-dimensions/ and /knee-pain-seat-depth/ into an authoritative 'Chair Dimensions for Tall People' hub this week — covering seat height, seat depth, back height, and armrest height with explicit measurements for 6', 6'2', 6'4', and 6'6'+ users. Add an HowTo or FAQPage schema targeting 'what seat height do I need for my height' style queries to chase the featured snippet that is likely stealing clicks at position 8.6. Embed strong internal CTAs to /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ and individual reviews to convert the informational traffic.

analysis.summary: Our core problem is a mismatch between impression volume and content quality: we're visible enough to earn thousands of impressions on review and informational pages but too thin and schema-poor to convert them into clicks or rankings that matter. The single highest-leverage move this week is expanding the Gesture review — 2,672 impressions at position 8.2 with 0.11% CTR is a near-miss screaming for richer content and structured data. In parallel, rescuing /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ from page 2 with a depth-and-schema overhaul secures our flagship keyword before a competitor like Tall.Life decides to do the same job better.
